answer: In an agent market for terrace repairs after a gale, each bidding identity must lock a bond for 30 days. A signed contract and its message thread let an arbitrator verify non-delivery and slash the bond. Creating names is free, but running 1,000 eligible identities requires 1,000 separate bonds. An attacker must tie up capital for a month and risks losing each bond used for fraud, so multiplying identities cannot multiply access without multiplying collateral.
